1. Aim

To containerize the existing frontend web application of the DES (Data Encryption Standard) Cryptography Virtual Lab using Docker; create an optimized production Dockerfile utilizing the official Nginx Alpine image; locally build and test the container on port 8080; push the version-tagged image (1.0) to the public Docker Hub registry; and pull and verify the published image as an independent container (des-lab-pulled) on port 8081.

2. Project Overview and Application Selection Justification

2.1 Project Overview

The DES Cryptography Virtual Lab is an interactive educational simulation designed for engineering students to explore symmetric-key cryptographic primitives. Key algorithmic components implemented include:

  • Single DES: Standard 16-round Feistel structure utilizing 64-bit plaintext blocks, 56-bit effective keys, non-linear S-Boxes for Confusion, and permutation matrices for Diffusion.
  • Double DES: Two sequential DES encryption passes, C = E(K2, E(K1, P)), illustrating how the Meet-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack reduces effective brute-force complexity from 2^112 down to 2^57.
  • Triple DES (3-Key EDE): The NIST SP 800-67 standard Encrypt-Decrypt-Encrypt architecture:
    • Encryption: C = E(K3, D(K2, E(K1, P))) with intermediate stages X1 = E(K1, P), X2 = D(K2, X1), and C = E(K3, X2).
    • Decryption: P = D(K1, E(K2, D(K3, C))) with intermediate stages Y1 = D(K3, C), Y2 = E(K2, Y1), and P = D(K1, Y2).
  • Interactive Frontend: Real-time browser calculation computing intermediate ciphertext blocks with client-side JavaScript (script.js) and cryptographic helpers (CryptoJS).

2.2 Justification for Containerization & Architecture Choice

  • Elimination of Environment Inconsistencies: Running web applications directly on local file systems (file:// URI scheme) frequently encounters browser security restrictions, path resolution disparities, and caching anomalies. Docker packages the application with a dedicated web server to ensure deterministic, zero-configuration execution.
  • High-Efficiency Web Server (Nginx Alpine): The application comprises static assets (index.html, style.css, script.js). The official nginx:alpine image provides a minimal attack surface and an ultra-lean footprint (~26 MB total size, ~9 MB compressed layer) without the runtime bloat of NodeJS or Python servers.
  • Direct Document Root Placement: The des/ directory was selected as the build context so that Nginx serves the virtual lab directly at root path /, removing unnecessary redirect loops and avoiding inclusion of root repository metadata (.git).

4. Dockerfile Configuration and Instruction Explanation

4.1 Dockerfile Implementation (des/Dockerfile)

FROM nginx:alpine

COPY . /usr/share/nginx/html

EXPOSE 80

CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"]

4.2 Instruction Breakdown

Instruction Function & Beginner-Friendly Explanation
FROM nginx:alpine Base Image: Specifies the foundation image. It uses Alpine Linux with Nginx pre-installed. Alpine is a tiny, secure Linux distro (~5 MB base), keeping the total container image lightweight and fast to download.
COPY . /usr/share/nginx/html Asset Copying: Transfers all frontend files (index.html, style.css, script.js) from the current folder into Nginx's default document root directory inside the container.
EXPOSE 80 Port Documentation: Informs Docker and administrators that the container listens on network port 80 (HTTP) at runtime.
CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"] Startup Command: Starts the Nginx server in the foreground. By default, Nginx runs in background daemon mode; running with daemon off; keeps process PID 1 running so Docker keeps the container active.

4.3 Docker Ignore Configuration (des/.dockerignore)

Dockerfile
.dockerignore
README.md

Purpose: Excludes non-runtime files (such as documentation and build configuration) from being copied into the final Nginx container image, keeping the image clean, compact, and secure.
